findings.issue: The 'migrated ledger row still reserves the id' assertion passes without any ledger row: the run was never terminal, so it has no runs.jsonl row to migrate, and ERR_RUN_EXISTS comes from machine.Init's run-directory check, not record.Exists.
findings.consequence: No CLI-level test shows a copied 0.13.x terminal row reserving its id; mis-wiring MigrateLegacyRows in roots() would pass this test.

findings.issue: LegacyRunsPending(root) is called on a non-git t.TempDir(), so StoreDir fails and it returns false without inspecting the .torn bookkeeping directory; the assertion cannot fail.
findings.consequence: The bookkeeping property is not exercised at the status layer (covered only by run.TestPendingLegacyRuns).

findings.issue: The out-of-repo case asserts only dir != "", which filepath.Join guarantees, and no test runs record-lenses --from-run end to end against a run found only in the 0.13.x store.
findings.consequence: A regression dropping the legacy warning or not passing the legacy dir to validateFromRunDiff goes unnoticed.

findings.issue: MigrateLegacyRows writes the legacy-ledger size stamp even when it found conflicting rows, so a ledger-row conflict is warned once and then suppressed, while a run-directory collision is re-warned on every fsm command with no remediation guidance.
findings.consequence: Operators miss the single ledger-conflict warning or get permanent collision noise; neither says how to resolve it.

findings.issue: The docs say plain `metareview status` lists any 0.13.x runs not yet migrated, but StatusLines only prints a count line naming the legacy directory, never the run ids (skills/fsm/SKILL.md has the same wording).
findings.consequence: An operator looking for a specific unmigrated run id in plain status output won't find it; cosmetic.

verdict.reasoning: The added assertion does not isolate ledger-row reservation: after migration, the same run directory exists in the common store, so duplicate initialization can return ERR_RUN_EXISTS even if runs.jsonl was absent or its migration were broken. toLegacy also silently skips the ledger when ReadFile fails. Thus the named ledger invariant is not pinned by this test. The broader claim that no other CLI test covers it is not independently supported by a repository-search record, but the defect in this specific assertion is directly visible in the diff.

The diff shows the call uses a non-git temporary directory, but it does not include the implementations of LegacyRunsPending or StoreDir, nor repository-search evidence establishing that this path necessarily returns false before inspecting .metareview/runs. Without that control-flow evidence, the claim that the assertion cannot fail, and the related coverage-absence claim, cannot be verified from the supplied material.

The supplied test record shows only unit-level checks of fromRunRunsDir for a legacy run. No record-lenses --from-run test exercises a run that exists solely in the 0.13.x store, so the caller could discard the returned warning or pass the common-store path to validateFromRunDiff and these tests would still pass. The out-of-repository assertion is also too weak to establish its named behavior: any nonempty, incorrect path satisfies it. The FSM migration test covers a different command path and does not close this record-lenses wiring gap.

The diff does claim that plain `metareview status` lists legacy 0.13.x runs, but no `StatusLines` implementation or sample output is provided. The proposed finding’s key premise—that status prints only a count and never run IDs—is therefore unverifiable from the supplied evidence and is speculation about code outside the diff.
